column1: # The time budget of every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, in minutes from the
# job's start to its end (time in the queue does not count).
# The required check "M0 language and kernel" runs scripts/ci-job-budgets.py on
# its own run and fails when a job took longer than its budget, so CI cannot
# creep back over the project's 20-minute rule unnoticed. A job that runs on
# pull requests ("pr") may have at most 17 minutes: that leaves three minutes
# for a slow runner. scripts/ci-job-budgets_test.sh checks that every job has
# exactly one budget here and that each budget fits under the job's
# Each budget is about 1.3 times the slowest of ten runs on 12 November 2026
# (five on main, five pull requests), within the ceiling. The two Native Go
# 1.27.3 jobs were one job then (21 to 22 minutes); their budgets come from that
# job's step times. Nightly jobs have their timeout-minutes as their budget.
# Raise a budget only in the pull request that makes the job slower, and say
# Columns, separated by tabs: minutes, scope (pr or nightly), the job's name as
# GitHub shows it, with * in place of a matrix value.
